newsitem.title: UK: American Airlines says filed writ against SW Trains.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines says filed writ against SW Trains.

text.p: AMR Corp's American Airlines, the U.S. transatlantic carrier, confirmed on Tuesday it has filed a writ against Stagecoach Holdings Plc's South West Trains over the rail company's use of the "Advantage" name for its frequent traveller programme.

American told Reuters "The case is not settled. A writ has been filed because they have been using a passenger loyalty programme with the same name as ours. We want to protect the name of our product," she said. American has refused to comment on whether it is seeking damages from SW Trains parent Stagecoach.

A spokeswoman for SW Trains said it was aware of the writ and added that the two parties had "reached an agreement in principle. But it is not finalised." American refused to confirm that any settlement had been reached, however.

The news comes as another damaging public relations blow to SW Trains, which has been slammed in the media for making dozens of cancellations to rail services since taking over the privatised rail franchise.

SW Trains' problems began after it made a large number of drivers redundant. The resulting train cancellations have angered passenger groups and the company is due to questioned by the parliamentary transport select committee next week.
American said its Advantage frequent flyer programme was a brand name in the U.S. and had a worldwide reputation which needed to be protected. It was first established in 1981.
